pr_title: drivers: ieee802154: cc13xx_cc26xx: raw mode support
pr_body:
This change adds IEEE802154_RAW_MODE support for the
cc1352r.

This allows using the cc1352r 2.4 GHz radio and Sub Ghz
radio as a transceiver (PHY) instead of using L2 networking.

Fixes #29951 

Signed-off-by: Erik Larson <erik@statropy.com>
pr_comments: @statropy - you might need to retrigger a build by either doing a `git commit --amend`, `git push --force` or possibly rebasing. Occasionally there are build failures due to documentation or unrelated build issues that slip through.

issue_context.title: ieee802154: cc13xx_cc26xx: raw mode support
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
The ieee802154 cc13xx_cc26xx 2.4 GHz and Sub GHz radios only support L2 networking. Adding raw mode would allow the radio to act as a PHY/transceiver to support running the MAC layer on an external host to allow a gateway application.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Remove dependency on any L2 networking settings and allow CONFIG_IEEE802154_RAW_MODE=y to be set when using the cc13xx_cc26xx.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

**Additional context**

review_comments:
Can you add a comment as to why this is necessary? A similar thing is done in the bed driver.

Also, just to understand better, when L2 is not enabled, what happens to the allocated network packets below here?
I'm ok with the PHY header being removed, since there is really no information gain from it. However, this variable should be renamed to 'mpdu' rather than 'psdu'.

Might be useful to use a similar structure that is used [here](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/drivers/ieee802154/ieee802154_nrf5.c#L120). Both in terms of the comment and the conditions, as it might make later refactorizations slightly easier.
